text: Land Encounters
Land Encounters And Points Of Interest fills the campaign map with places worth a detour. Almost everything it adds sits on the map as a marker your lords can walk onto.
What You Will Find
[[sl:land_enc_encounters]]Encounter spots[[/sl]] hold a battle or a treasure site. They come and go across every map zone.
An [[sl:land_enc_towers]]Ancient Tower[[/sl]] stands in each map zone. Climb it floor by floor for a growing haul.
[[sl:land_enc_smithies]]Smithies[[/sl]] and [[sl:land_enc_taverns]]Taverns[[/sl]] can be claimed and held. They offer items, mercenaries, contracts and services.
Your lords bring home lasting [[sl:land_enc_boons_and_curses]]boons and curses[[/sl]], and your armies can win [[sl:land_enc_army_spells]]army spells[[/sl]].
Getting Started

Send a lord in the default, channelling or ambush stance onto any marker. A dilemma always shows what is on offer before anything is spent, and almost every choice can be turned down. Early fights are easy. Enemies grow stronger from turn 15, and again from turn 25.
Making It Your Own
Every feature can be tuned or turned off in the mod's settings, which also hold a guide to every offer. See [[sl:land_enc_settings]]Settings and Compatibility[[/sl]].

Encounter Spots
Encounter spots are the markers scattered across each map zone. Walk a lord onto one to find out what it holds: a battle, or a treasure site.
How Spots Appear
Each map zone keeps about 75% of its spots active at a time.
A spot nobody visits fades after 10 turns. A used spot stays empty for 5 turns before the zone fills up again.
When a lord steps on, the spot is a battle 70% of the time. Otherwise it is a [[sl:land_enc_treasure]]treasure site[[/sl]].
Only a lord in the default, channelling or ambush stance can use a spot. Anyone else just gets a message.
Battles
A battle spot opens a dilemma naming the enemy and their faction. Choose Fight, or Avoid to walk away. Avoiding costs no gold, but some foes leave a parting gift that lingers for a few turns.
Fights come in kinds, from a Skirmish or Bandits up to a Battlefield or a Daemonic Gift. The rarer kinds turn up more often on higher difficulties.
Some fights are an Ally in Peril: an ally's army is beset beside you, or needs a relief column. Saving them improves [[img:icon_diplomacy]][[/img]] relations with their kin.
Winning pays [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold and, for most fights, an item. Hard fights have a 5% chance of a legendary item.
A battle can also come with offers, missions and twists. See [[sl:land_enc_battle_events]]Battle Offers and Missions[[/sl]].
Difficulty

Enemies start Easy, become Medium from turn 15 and Hard from turn 25. Their armies are built from a gold budget and an army recipe, so a fight can be a shield wall, a monster horde or a gunline. The Enemy Forces page of the mod's settings changes both.
AI Factions
AI lords use spots too. They take a flat reward of gold, and sometimes an item, instead of fighting.
Map markers that hold a battle or a treasure site.

Battle Offers and Missions
Many battle spots come with extra choices before the fight, and some fights carry a twist of their own.
Pre-Battle Offers

30% of battle dilemmas also offer 2 ways to tip the fight: bribe guards, thin the enemy's ranks, hire allies, bless your banners or raise the stakes for a bigger prize. Each choice shows its price, in [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold, blood or risk. One you cannot afford is shown greyed out.
Missions
The same dilemma can offer 2 missions: optional goals like keeping your lord alive or killing their champion.
Taking a mission opens the dilemma again, so you can take several before you fight.
Each mission met in a won battle pays its reward. Failing one usually costs nothing, but a few vows carry a curse.
Missions are only judged in a battle you fight yourself. If you auto-resolve, none count, and any wager comes back.
Battle Modifiers

Each fight has a 5% chance to roll battle modifiers: storms, last stands, enemy heroes, whole armies of a faction's famous units and more. Some help you, some hurt you, and some cut both ways. A harmful modifier raises the victory gold and a helpful one lowers it. The dilemma lists them before you choose.
Spoils of War
After a won battle, there is a 30% chance to pick from the spoils: loot, prisoners, captured spells and more, or simply the gold.
In Battle

When a fight carries buffs, missions or modifiers, a button beside the menu bar shows or hides the objectives panel that tracks them. In a battle beside an allied army, your reinforcements may arrive sooner than usual.
Offers, missions and twists that can come with a battle.

Treasure Sites
When an encounter spot is not a battle, it is a treasure site: one of 16 kinds of place, each with a story of its own.
How a Site Works
Every site has its own special offer, plus 2 more drawn from the treasure and realm offers. Offers that suit the site come up more often.
Take one, or Walk away for nothing. Prices in [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold rise with the encounter difficulty.
Some offers cost more than gold: a curse, a tougher next fight, worse [[img:icon_diplomacy]][[/img]] relations, or a battle with a guardian.
Kinds of Offer
Treasure: gold, items, [[sl:land_enc_army_spells]]army spells[[/sl]], [[sl:land_enc_boons_and_curses]]boons[[/sl]], and pacts that trade a curse for a stronger boon.
Realm: offers that reach beyond the army, like improving a region, sending gifts to a friend or hiring raiders against an enemy. Each names its target before you choose.
Guardians: wake a sleeping champion for a unique item, if you can beat it.
The Sites

Hidden Tomb, Abandoned Camp, Buried Relics, Hidden Temple, Caravan Remnants, A Voice in the Dream, The Explorers, Legendary Bard, Ruined Shrine, Smugglers' Cache, Beast Lair, Old Battlefield, Witch's Hut, Collapsed Mine, Merchant's Wagon and Sunken Library.
AI Factions
AI lords take a flat reward of gold, an item and a short blessing instead.
Encounter spots that hold treasure, offers and the odd guardian.

Ancient Towers
One ancient tower stands in each map zone, held by a random faction. Delve it floor by floor for a growing haul, if your army can survive the climb.
The Climb
Walk a lord onto a tower and choose Enter the Tower. Each of its 5 floors is a battle somewhere new on the map.
Each floor won adds [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold and items to the haul. The fewer men you lose, the more the floor pays.
From floor 3, some of the beaten army's units swear themselves to you. The last floor holds the tower's master, guarding legendary items.
Between Floors

After each win, pick one of up to 4 offers to help the climb, or leave with the haul. Offers range from healing and fresh troops to [[sl:land_enc_army_spells]]army spells[[/sl]], a sealed vault, a hidden floor, or a champion to fight for a [[sl:land_enc_boons_and_curses]]boon[[/sl]]. Some are pacts with a price.
Losing and Leaving
Losing a floor loses the whole haul. Units already sworn to you stay.
Leaving pays the haul in full. Beating the master lets you claim the tower's treasure.
After any delve, the tower closes for 5 turns, then passes to a new faction.
Champions

A champion floor pits you against a legendary lord. Win it and your lord picks a boon, with a 3% chance to bless your whole faction for 5 turns instead. Lose it, and there is the same chance of a curse on your faction.
A tower in each map zone to climb for a growing haul.

Smithies
Smithies are forges scattered across the map. Claim one and its master smith works for you: free gear, work orders for your army, and help with your boons and curses.
Claiming and Holding
Walk a lord onto an unclaimed Smithy to claim it for free.

A Smithy held by anyone else must be taken by beating its garrison, which is tougher at higher levels. Taking one from a faction you are not at war with costs 20 [[img:icon_diplomacy]][[/img]] relations with them.
Enemies at war with you can besiege your Smithy. Fight them with its garrison, or surrender it. A Smithy you lose drops a level.
The Forge
Take one of 2 free items, of better rarity at higher forge levels. The forge then cools for 5 turns or more.
While it cools, Rush the Forge ends the wait for 500 [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold per turn left, times the forge level.
Work Orders offer 3 orders for the whole army for a few turns, like heavier plate or honed edges. Taking one closes the counter for 5 turns.
Commission a masterwork, or upgrade the forge for better items, a shorter cooldown and more frequent tribute.
Temper and Break

At a Smithy you own, the smith tempers a boon one level or breaks a curse, for gold per level. Trade Rust for Iron gives a boon and a curse together, for free. See [[sl:land_enc_boons_and_curses]]Boons and Curses[[/sl]].
Owning a Smithy
Your Smithies send you an item as tribute every few turns. A level 3 forge sometimes sends a legendary one.
While you hold both a Smithy and its region, Arms Trade raises the province's [[img:icon_income]][[/img]] income and the Garrison Armoury arms its garrison.

Every 10 turns, your best Smithy offers a Smith's Commission: a kill count, beating armies of your nearest enemy, or winning at a marked spot, for an item named on the mission. Failing one costs nothing.
The Smiths' Association

A Generous Donation of 50000 [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold at your own forge raises every Smithy to at least level 2, and blesses your armies' weapons for good. A second donation of 100000 gold raises every Smithy to level 3 and doubles the blessing.
Forges to claim for free items, work orders and smithing services.

Taverns
Each map zone has two Taverns: one run by a single race, and a neutral house open to all. Hire swords, try your luck at the bar, take contracts and visit the hedge-witch.
Claiming and Visiting
Walk a lord onto an unclaimed Tavern to claim it, onto your own to open it, or onto an ally's or a neutral one to visit as a guest.
Any Tavern you do not own can be taken by beating its garrison. Taking one from a faction you are not at war with costs 20 [[img:icon_diplomacy]][[/img]] relations.
Enemies at war with you can besiege yours. A Tavern you lose drops a level.
The Mercenary Hall
Hire units of the Tavern's race, famous regiments, a hero and a few units of your own kind. A neutral Tavern stocks two races, picked at random.
Each costs its [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] recruitment cost plus 1000 gold. A veteran company costs half again as much, and a cut-price sellsword costs half but arrives at a quarter of its strength.
You can hire 2 per visit, then the hall closes to your faction for 5 turns. The stock changes every 5 turns.
The Bar

Three drinks and games are on offer each visit, each a gamble or a short-lived boost. Prices rise with the campaign's difficulty, and the owner pays a quarter less. Taking one closes the bar to your faction for 5 turns.
The Contract Board
The Tavern Keepers' Guild posts bounties, culls and marked spots, and a three-step quest at level 3. Each takes a deposit, which comes back with the reward.

You can hold 1 contract at a time. Fail or drop one and you lose the deposit, and every Guild Tavern charges you 25% more for 10 turns. Buying a contract out returns half the deposit, with no surcharge.
Hazard pay offers half again the gold for one more harmful battle modifier. Contract terms add a bonus mission to the fight.
The Hedge-Witch

The hedge-witch cleanses a curse or gambles on one, feeds a boon toward its next level, reweaves a boon, or lifts a curse with a blood rite paid in your army's strength. See [[sl:land_enc_boons_and_curses]]Boons and Curses[[/sl]].
The Tavern Keepers' Guild

A Generous Donation of 50000 [[img:icon_money]][[/img]] gold at any Tavern raises every Tavern to at least level 2 and ends the Guild's surcharge for you. It also blesses your faction's [[img:icon_income]][[/img]] income, trade and armies for good, with [[img:icon_experience]][[/img]] experience for every lord and hero each turn. A second donation of 100000 gold raises every Tavern to level 3 and doubles the blessing.
Taverns to claim for mercenaries, drinks, contracts and the hedge-witch.

Boons and Curses
A lord can carry lasting boons and curses. Each one is a trait on the lord, whose levels you can hover to see what they do, and an icon in the army's effects says when it next changes.
How Boons Grow
A boon grows one level for every 5 battles the lord wins, up to level 5. Lost battles never take a level away.
A charged boon does not grow. It lasts a set number of battles, then fades.
Gaining a boon the lord already has raises it a level, or refills its charges.
How Curses Grow
A curse worsens one level every 5 turns, up to level 5.
Some curses turn into a boon after 10 turns at their worst. The rest stay until lifted.
When the lord has no room for another curse, the mildest one worsens instead.
Slots
A lord has 3 boon slots and 3 curse slots. A new boon on a lord with every slot full asks which one to give up. A lord who dies or leaves the faction loses them all, and AI lords get none.
Where They Come From
A hard or modified win has a 3% chance to leave a boon, and a lost battle or failed contract a 3% chance to leave a curse. Each battle modifier has a 3% chance to linger as one.

Pacts at [[sl:land_enc_treasure]]treasure sites[[/sl]], the [[sl:land_enc_taverns]]Tavern[[/sl]] bar and the [[sl:land_enc_towers]]Towers[[/sl]] trade a curse for a stronger boon. Tower champions and Tavern contracts give boons too.
A Tower champion floor can bless or curse your whole faction for 5 turns. These take no lord's slot.
Lifting Curses and Raising Boons
At a [[sl:land_enc_smithies]]Smithy[[/sl]] you own, the smith tempers a boon one level or breaks a curse.
At any [[sl:land_enc_taverns]]Tavern[[/sl]], the hedge-witch cleanses a curse or gambles on one, feeds or reweaves a boon, or lifts a curse with a blood rite.
These are the default numbers. The Boons and Curses page of the mod's settings changes them.
Lasting blessings and burdens your lords carry from fight to fight.

Army Spells
An army spell lets an army cast a spell or ability in battle without spending the Winds of Magic, whoever leads it.
How They Work
An army spell shows on the army as an effect, naming the spell and how many casts it has in each battle.
Lore spells give 1 to 3 casts, more for cheaper spells. Bound spells and army abilities keep their own uses.
Most last 5 turns. Some last only for the next battle.
Over 400 can turn up, from every lore of magic, bound item and army ability in the game.
Where to Find Them
[[sl:land_enc_treasure]]Treasure sites[[/sl]]: scrolls, shrines and runestones.
[[sl:land_enc_battle_events]]Battles[[/sl]]: pre-battle scrolls, the Witch Hunt mission and the spoils of war.
[[sl:land_enc_taverns]]Taverns[[/sl]]: the Spell Pedlar at the bar, and won marked-spot contracts.
[[sl:land_enc_smithies]]Smithies[[/sl]]: the Runesmith's Inscription work order.
[[sl:land_enc_towers]]Towers[[/sl]]: scrolls, relics and war horns between floors, for the next floor.

Settings and Compatibility
Everything in Land Encounters can be tuned through the Mod Configuration Tool (MCT). Each feature has its own page, with an in-game guide to how it works and what every offer does.
Settings Pages
General: how many spots are active, and how many are battles.
Encounters: battle types, event chances, marker skins, and guides to every offer.
Enemy Forces: difficulty, budgets, army recipes, and units from other mods.
Towers, Smithies, Taverns, and Boons and Curses: each can be tuned or turned off. Smithies and Taverns can be removed from the map.
Changes to the Base Game
Dilemma layout: a dilemma with more than three rows of choices, or one too tall for your screen, shows its choices in a scrolling list. This applies to every dilemma in the game.
Battle scripts: the mod's battle scripts load in every battle, but only act in its own fights.
Objectives button: in the mod's fights that carry buffs, missions or modifiers, a button beside the menu bar shows or hides the objectives panel.
Good to Know
Works in Immortal Empires, the Realm of Chaos and The Old World, and with Immortal Empires Expanded.
Multiplayer is untested.
